record.file_problem: Repository README and file list only; the other listed files and result artifacts were not read. The README is not stated to be garbled or cut off.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports behavioral outcomes after refusal-ablating weight edits on released Qwen models. This tests practical removal (V2), but does not apply the original difference-in-means activation projection.
record.gate_note: The README reports refusal/compliance rates for the edited models, which are recorded below. It also gives per-item counts (141-0, 132-0, 83-1, 28-0, and 32-19) without identifying their model, benchmark, or precise measure in the README; these are not assigned to rows. The file list alone does not establish results.
record.test_reason: It measures harmful-request compliance and XSTest refusal for stock versus abliterated weight-edited Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen3.8-27B builds. That bears directly on V2 (practical removal) in a new setting: new models, community tools OBLITERATUS and Heretic, and a rubric judge instead of a substring matcher. It does not compute or ablate a difference-in-means direction itself.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but it omits the headline claim and two others. The headline is that abliteration gets more dangerous as base models improve: the base model, not the recipe, explains about 4x higher StrongREJECT compliance on Qwen3.8. The authors also say ablation has a nested per-item signature unlike prompt attacks, which they call their most novel contribution. And they say substring-matcher '0/100 refusals' claims are not comparable to rubric-judged rates. They report no capability uplift ('unlocks willingness, not ability').
record.recipe_differences: Repository is an evaluation project comparing practical refusal-ablating weight edits (OBLITERATUS and Heretic), not a reported reproduction of the original activation-projection method.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by model generation, ablation recipe, and benchmark: the README reports a generation effect on StrongREJECT and a recipe effect on XSTest unsafe items. It also reports a Qwen3.6 OBLITERATUS template confound and changed Qwen3.8 Heretic XSTest results after frontier-judge regrading.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-item comparisons are near-perfectly nested for ablation (141-0, 132-0, 83-1, 28-0) but not for a published prompt attack (32-19). The authors read this as ablation lowering one threshold, while the prompt attack perturbs items.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-edit ablation and prompt jailbreaks change refusal with different per-item signatures, so they may not act on refusal the same way.

fits_no_version.finding: The README asserts no capability uplift across three tasks after ablation, without values.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal ablation does not increase task capability.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the same class of edit, Qwen3.8 shows about 4x higher StrongREJECT compliance than Qwen3.6 (108-vs-4 discordant pairs, p=2.5e-27).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How far abliteration removes refusal depends on the base model generation.

record.problems: The README is self-reported repository material; underlying files and results were not read. Capability outcomes are summarized without task names or values. The StrongREJECT judge is not identified in the README excerpt. The README itself flags a Qwen3.6 OBLITERATUS template confound and says XSTest coverage and regrading changed results.
record.rows_left_out: Per-item counts 141-0, 132-0, 83-1, 28-0, and 32-19 were not entered as rows because the README excerpt does not identify their model, benchmark, or exact measure. The README says capability tasks have n=30–80 but does not provide individual task results.

untested.parts: Only two community recipes (OBLITERATUS, Heretic), only two Qwen 27B generations, and only Q4_K_M quantisation. Capability preservation relative to stock is not reported with values. Whether the recipes implement the original difference-in-means edit is not established.
No direction is extracted, ablated or added in activations.
No test of whether prompt attacks suppress the direction, and no adversarial training. Only an unlabelled per-item contrast between ablation and a prompt attack is given.
Generation differences are reported, but training is not varied or characterised.

missing.what: Statistic that a substring-matcher refusal scorer (markers include 'illegal', 'harmful') underlies published '0/100 refusals' claims, versus 43.3% compliance under a rubric judge. This bears on how V2 removal is measured.

record.verdict_notes: Self-published GitHub README; underlying result files were not read. The 'Qwen3.6/3.8' names are taken as given. Removal is clearly incomplete under a rubric judge: at most about 46% compliance on StrongREJECT. This is the main reason V2 is labelled limits_scope rather than supports. The Qwen3.6 OBLITERATUS arm is confounded by an injected system prompt.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction is found, projected out, or added.
Tests weight edits on the listed Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen3.8-27B builds only; other model families and edit recipes are not established.
Does not test whether attacks suppress the refusal direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
Does not test whether refusal is carried by an affine set, cone, or multiple directions.
Does not separate harmfulness judgment from refusal.
Does not test transfer across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
Does not vary refusal training or test when refusal is trained.

tranche.reason: It tests V2 (weight-edit abliteration removes refusal) in a new setting: new Qwen3.6/3.8-27B models, released community builds (OBLITERATUS, Heretic), and a StrongREJECT rubric judge plus XSTest. It reports refusal and compliance rates for these settings. Its argument about substring scoring adds a T5-like element, but T3 fits best.

source_check.notes: The text is only the repo README and file list. The fuller results (HO3-RESULTS.md, eval-results-technical-paper.md) are not in the text. The OBLITERATUS confound applies only to the Qwen3.6 build. Judges are local 27B-Q4 unless stated, and the DeepSeek-v4-pro judge matches StrongREJECT headlines within ~1 point. The authors' headline is that abliteration is ~4x more effective on Qwen3.8 than on Qwen3.6, with no capability uplift, so 'later Qwen resists' groupings misread it.

statements.correction: StrongREJECT, 313 prompts, Q4_K_M. Qwen3.6-27B: stock 0.0%, Heretic 9.0% (clean arm), OBLITERATUS 16.5% (confounded by a template-injected anti-refusal system prompt that biases toward compliance). Qwen3.8-27B: stock 0.0%, OBLITERATUS 45.7%, Heretic 43.3%. Authors: edit ~4x more effective on Qwen3.8; generational effect 108-vs-4, p = 2.5e-27; recipe difference on Qwen3.8 p = 0.43.
statements.problem: The numbers are right, but listing this study as evidence that later Qwen models 'resist' edits misreads it. Its headline is the opposite trend: the newer Qwen3.8 is much more affected than Qwen3.6. About 44% compliance on Qwen3.8 is substantial, not resistance. Its per-study verdicts are limits_scope, not challenges.

statements.correction: Qwen3.8-27B StrongREJECT compliance: 0.0% stock, 43.3% Heretic, 45.7% OBLITERATUS (local judge, 27B-Q4 unless stated). XSTest unsafe refusal (DeepSeek-v4-pro frontier judge, coverage 192-250): 84.3% stock, 53.9% Heretic, 33.9% OBLITERATUS. The template confound is stated only for qwen3.6-27b-obliteratus (round 1); the README does not state one for the Qwen3.8 arms.
statements.problem: 'Its OBLITERATUS arm has a template confound' sits in a statement about Qwen3.8 builds. The README attributes the confound only to the Qwen3.6 OBLITERATUS GGUF (round 1). The XSTest numbers also come from a different judge (frontier, DeepSeek-v4-pro) than the StrongREJECT local rubric judge.

statements.correction: Confound is on the qwen3.6-27b-obliteratus GGUF only; injects the prompt whenever the caller sends no system prompt; biases toward compliance.
statements.problem: Correct for the README: it flags the Qwen3.6 OBLITERATUS chat template that injects an anti-refusal system prompt, and reports no system-prompt-varied results. However, the file list includes regrade files such as 'obliterated-responsible_assistant.json' and 'normal-responsible_assistant.json'. These may hold prompt or system-prompt variants that the text does not show.

statements.correction: Point 5: the reference tool (Heretic) scores refusal with a 41-marker substring matcher; a Heretic build scores 43.3% compliance under a rubric judge. No matcher score for that build is given. On the same generations, the DeepSeek-v4-pro frontier judge matches StrongREJECT headline numbers within ~1 point (Cohen's kappa 0.87-1.00). The frontier re-grade of XSTest raised coverage to 193/200 and moved Heretic-3.8 unsafe refusal from 69.5% to 53.9%.
statements.problem: The factor is 'same generations, different judges', but the README gives no substring-matcher score on its own generations. The 0/100 contrast is with published claims, not a paired re-scoring. The README also gives same-generation judge evidence that the statement omits.
